data.narrative:
Fulfil is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $127M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-stage, same-sector comparables (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, and Dexterity) alongside a broader universe of eight private robotics firms and one public comparable.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $127M total raised as a valuation proxy, yielding $241M. The peer-median method anchors to the median valuation of the three direct comparables at $1.8B, with a range spanning $1.6B (Dexterity) to $2.0B (Generalist AI). These peers represent the most granular match on sector and stage.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $205M to $2.0B, with a median cross-section of $996M. The wide dispersion reflects material methodological divergence: stage-progression anchors to capital raised and assumes incremental value creation, while peer-median reflects market pricing of functionally similar Series B robotics companies. Key uncertainties include the relevance of the peer set given heterogeneity in robotics subsectors, the comparability of capital efficiency across the three direct comps, and whether Fulfil's positioning within the robotics market justifies upside or downside to peer-median valuation. The public market comparable (277810.KQ) was not heavily weighted given limited direct sector overlap.
